questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Brussels?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Belgium is Brussels.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Belgium about 30,688 square kilometres; Dominica about 751 square kilometres; Malta about 316 square kilometres; Liechtenstein about 161 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Belgium on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Belgium on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belgium?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belgium article.

questions.proof: Its capital, Brussels, is the home of many organizations, including the European Union and NATO.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belgium?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belgium on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belgium article.

questions.proof: Belgium is bordered by the Netherlands in the north, Germany to the east, Luxembourg to the southeast and France to the south.
